clue.text: It's difficult to reproduce a computer printout

blocks.note: hard means difficult
to copy is to reproduce something

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that making a duplicate of a printed computer sheet is tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard copy is the term for information printed on paper rather than held on a screen.

clue.text: Mix chocolates, for example, with potato dish

blocks.note: a hash is a jumbled mix
chocolate is one of the browns, shades of colour

explanation.surface: A cook stirs boxed sweets into a potato recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chocolates' means the colours, not the sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash browns are grated fried potato cakes, a breakfast side served in diners.

clue.text: Celebrating noisily, because "Rose" tour is off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of place, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fans party loudly because a show called Rose has had its tour cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Because' is only a link; the three words before 'off' supply every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Roistering means revelling boisterously, so a roisterous crowd is partying with lots of noise.

clue.text: Sparing tears, embracing laughter

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside the arms, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to shed tears is to cry
ha is the sound of a laugh

explanation.surface: Someone holds back weeping while hugging amid merriment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chary of something means being cautious or sparing with it, slow to give.

clue.text: Best point at which to start a race in cold climates?

definitions.text: Best point at which to start a race

blocks.clueFragment: Best point at which to start a race
blocks.note: first meaning: the front slot on a motor-racing grid
second, playful meaning: a location at the North or South Pole

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a 'position' at a 'pole' is where the cold climates are, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pole position is the leading grid place earned by the fastest qualifier in motor racing.

clue.text: Almost entirely encrusted with sugar -- honest!

indicators.note: almost entirely means not quite the whole thing, so one letter must go

blocks.note: fruit coated in a crust of sugar is candied

explanation.surface: A confectioner frankly admits something is almost completely coated in sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: CANDIED loses one E to give CANDID; here the dropped letter is not the last one, which is unusual for 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A candid person speaks frankly and openly, so the adjective is a direct synonym for truthful.

clue.text: Re-written note meant to make amends?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the act of making amends

indicators.note: something rewritten is put down again differently, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A redrafted letter intended as an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is reparation for a wrong, the act of putting things right.

clue.text: Money owing on a 500 bet, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so the letters can be reordered

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gambler might end up owing money on a five-hundred wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is a sum that one person owes to another.

clue.text: Double act getting the bird

blocks.note: to do is to act; doubled, it appears twice

explanation.surface: A comedy duo is booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' is the theatre idiom for being jeered, which hides the real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a large flightless bird of Mauritius, extinct since the seventeenth century.

clue.text: It's OK to be fit and strong

blocks.note: to suit is to fit or be right for
able-bodied, capable and strong

explanation.surface: A reassurance that it is fine to be healthy and powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable or appropriate for the purpose is fine, all right, adequate.

clue.text: In favour of tender giving rise to veto

blocks.note: for means supporting
a tender is a formal offer, a bid

explanation.surface: Backing a contract offer somehow leads to it being blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an adjective meaning gentle, but it is the noun for an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to refuse permission, prohibit it outright.

clue.text: Cheat theatre assistant over item of furniture

blocks.note: to welsh is to cheat by not paying a debt
a dresser helps actors into costume

explanation.surface: A swindler gets the better of a backstage helper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh dresser is a wooden sideboard topped with open shelves for displaying plates.

clue.text: Main observation chamber has tub, last of luxury range

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of the following word only

blocks.note: a bath is a tub
the final letter of the word
a sphere of influence is a range or scope

explanation.surface: A luxury product line includes a main viewing room with its own bathtub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the old poetic word for the sea, not 'principal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathysphere is a spherical diving vessel lowered into the deep sea for watching marine life.

clue.text: Flags flying around another dam, showing discourtesy

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed on both sides of the other
another version means a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: banners are flags flown aloft
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Banners wave around a second reservoir wall in a rude display.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad manners is rude, impolite behaviour, the opposite of courtesy.

clue.text: Flirts with Greek character? Dreadful slander!

indicators.note: dreadful means badly done, so the letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone protests that being called a womaniser is a slur on a Greek's good name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who philanders has casual affairs with women, flirting without commitment.

clue.text: Monsters love note about son

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
G is a musical note
re means about or concerning
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Fearsome creatures adore a letter concerning their boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, the classic fairy-tale beasts.

clue.text: Pays up for casings that are no longer "in"

blocks.note: shells are hard outer casings
out is the opposite of in, or unfashionable

explanation.surface: Someone spends money on cases that have gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelling out is an informal phrase for handing over money, often reluctantly.

clue.text: She scans a suspect, who's not a Scot

indicators.note: a suspect account is dubious and not to be taken as given, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman at a border scrutinises a suspicious person who is evidently not Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is the Scots term, often mildly hostile, for an English person or any outsider to Scotland.

clue.text: Sick ass left Nassau before being mounted

indicators.note: left here means departed, so that word goes out of the place name

blocks.note: the letters that depart
the capital of the Bahamas
a mounted rider is seated on the horse

explanation.surface: A poorly donkey quit the Bahamas before anyone could ride it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction or a political side, but here it means departed: the animal walks out of the capital's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling nauseated means feeling queasy and ready to vomit, which is being ill.

clue.text: Indian to get a million rupees, or some of it

indicators.note: some of it tells us only a part of the phrase before is wanted, read straight through

blocks.note: found running across the words get a million

explanation.surface: An Indian person stands to receive a huge sum in rupees, or a share of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so one is an Indian.

clue.text: Unpredictable element may free churchman, they say

indicators.note: they say means as people pronounce it, so we go by the spoken form

blocks.note: loose means free, untied
a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: Someone might release a cleric, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: CANON, the cleric, is pronounced like CANNON, the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cannon is a person whose erratic behaviour makes them a danger to their own side.

clue.text: Perform on horseback and cause trouble!

blocks.note: to act is to perform
a jockey who is up is riding

explanation.surface: A circus rider does tricks in the saddle and creates havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or play up, being difficult on purpose.

clue.text: Return of a bad French priest

indicators.note: return means going back the way one came, so the words are read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
mal is French for bad

explanation.surface: A wicked French clergyman comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet, a religious leader.

clue.text: Goes back into each building by sundown initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone returns indoors to every house before dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it recedes, flowing away from the shore.

clue.text: Wayward albino came to Britain once

indicators.note: wayward means straying off course, so these letters stray from their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wandering pale-skinned traveller arrived on British shores long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is the ancient, now poetic, name for the island of Great Britain.

clue.text: You and I get right into a site, so to speak

indicators.note: these pieces get into the following phrase, placed inside it

blocks.note: you and I together are we
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people secure the right of entry to a plot of land, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are verbal hedges meaning in a manner of speaking, not literally.

clue.text: Advantages that flow from TESSAs

indicators.note: to flow is to move fluidly, so the letters run into a fresh order

blocks.note: a TESSA was a tax-exempt special savings account in Britain

explanation.surface: Benefits that come from holding a particular kind of savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are useful qualities or resources, things that work in one's favour.

clue.text: Suggests partnership based on professional attitudes

blocks.note: pro is short for professional
a pose or attitude is a bodily posture

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a business partnership grounded in a businesslike outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attitudes' looks like opinions, but here it means physical postures.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to ask someone to marry, offering a lifelong union.
